newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg's Boliden to set up j/v miner.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg's Boliden to set up j/v miner.

text.p: Swedish metals and mining group Trelleborg's Boliden unit said on Monday it would set up a new mining company together with Swedish businessman Adolf Lundin and list it on the Stockholm bourse in the spring.
The new company, North Atlantic Natural Resources (NAN), would be listed on the Stockholm bourse's O-list, Boliden said in a statement.
NAN will be owned in equal parts by Lundin's company South Atlantic Resources (SCQ) and Boliden. It will operate in Sweden, Norway, Finland and north-west Russia.
Boliden said NAN's main aim was to identify and develop gold and other precious metals deposits.
Base metal potential throughout the area was also judged to be good.
SCQ and Boliden agreed on a right of first refusal for Boliden to acquire, at market value, a minimum of 51 percent ownership stake in base metal finds, Boliden said.
Boliden will transfer prospecting concessions for 70,000-80,000 hectares in the Swedish areas of Norbotten, Skellefteafaltet and Bergslagen to the new company, it said.
SCQ will transfer prospecting concessions, of a corresponding size, which they recently bought from the Swedish company Svenska Miljo och Mineral.
The two companies also planned a new share issue worth over 100 million crowns in conjunction with the listing of the new company, Lundin told a news conference.
"We have not decided exactly how large it will be but it will certainly be over 100 million crowns," Lundin said.
NAN will be a separate company with separate financing, the companies said.
During the first years, NAN's investments are expected to total 40-70 million crowns.
Boliden's own prospecting volume would not be significantly affected by the creation of the new company, Bulow said.
